newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: KEDO to start building reactors in N.Korea Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: KEDO to start building reactors in N.Korea Aug 19.

text.p: A consortium of nations building two nuclear reactors in impoverished North Korea said on Thursday that actual construction of the plants would begin next week.

A statement from the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organisation's (KEDO) office in Seoul said the ground-breaking ceremony would be held at 2:00 p.m. (0500 GMT) next Tuesday in the northeastern town of Sinpo.
KEDO, which includes the United States, South Korea and Japan, was formed in 1995 to finance the building of two light-water reactors according to a 1994 agreement between Pyongyang and Washington.
The agreement, signed in Geneva, was designed to halt North Korea's suspected nuclear weapons programme.
Government representatives from the U.S., South Korea, Japan and other KEDO member countries would attend the ground-breaking ceremony, the statement said.

Last month KEDO opened a liaison office in Sinpo to oversee the project, and South Korean vessels carrying 9,000 tonnes of bulldozers, trucks and heavy equipment have arrived in North Korea to clear land at the site of the project.
The ground-breaking ceremony coincides with efforts to bring peace to the Korean peninsula and growing fears that chronic food shortages in North Korea will worsen.

Officials of the two Koreas, the United States and China met in New York last week to set an agenda for formal peace talks but failed to reach an agreement. They are due to try again on September 15 in New York.
The four-nation talks, proposed by Seoul and Washington last year, aim to set up a permanent peace mechanism on the Korean peninsula, the last flashpoint of the Cold War.
North and South Korea remain technically at war as their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce and not a peace treaty.
